execution.description: Smart-contract / execution layers are judged primarily on fee-generating usage and developer activity.

monetary.description: Monetary assets are NOT judged primarily on protocol revenue. Milestone achievement (surviving cycles, institutional adoption) dominates; fees measure settlement demand.

oracle.description: Oracle networks are judged on feed adoption and fee-paying data consumers; TVL is mostly irrelevant.

payments.description: Payment rails are judged on settlement volume and institutional dependence; speculation-free usage matters most.

changelog: v0.2.0 adds Potential Outlook (a forward-looking but explicitly uncalibrated derived metric: how much of the unrealized promise current execution supports capturing — NOT a probability, NOT a price prediction) and a published observer-effect policy: the Clock acknowledges that publishing scores can itself move markets (reflexivity) and commits to safeguards — append-only history, versioned methodology, publisher holdings disclosure, no per-project tuning, no paid placement.

capital_committed.description: How much capital is committed onchain (TVL). Log-scaled: $10M -> 0, $100B -> 10.
capital_committed.name: Capital committed

developer_activity.description: Core-protocol development pace. CoinGecko developer_data in v0.1 (spotty upstream); dedicated GitHub adapter is Phase 2.
developer_activity.name: Developer activity

economic_throughput.description: Trailing user-paid fee revenue, annualized. Fees are the hardest evidence of willingness to pay for blockspace.
economic_throughput.name: Economic throughput

incentive_dependence.description: Share of activity attributable to token incentives. No reliable Phase 1 source.
incentive_dependence.name: Incentive dependence

milestone_velocity.description: Thesis milestones achieved in the trailing 3 years, scaled: 2+ milestones -> 10. Momentum, not just level.
milestone_velocity.name: Milestone velocity

necessity_inverse.description: 10 minus analyst-assessed Token Necessity. A token the protocol does not need is a reflexive-asset warning sign.
necessity_inverse.name: Token-necessity inverse

setback_drag.description: Major setbacks (outages, failed launches, lost flagship deals) in the trailing 3 years. Each setback subtracts 3 points from 10.
setback_drag.name: Setback drag

supply_overhang.description: Share of fully-diluted value not yet circulating: (FDV - market cap) / FDV * 10. Future dilution is future sell pressure.
supply_overhang.name: Supply overhang

thesis_milestones.description: Highest achieved rung (0-5) of the category milestone ladder, scaled to 0-10. Analyst-assessed against published evidence requirements.
thesis_milestones.name: Thesis milestones

valuation_multiple.description: log10(market_cap / annualized_fees), mapped so a 10x multiple -> 2 and a 100,000x multiple -> 10. Answers: how much of today's value is explained by today's economic activity?
valuation_multiple.name: Valuation vs economic activity

confidence.method: 100 * mean over dimensions of (available_weight_fraction * source_quality). Measured components have quality 1.0, analyst-assessed 0.75. Never claims 100%: the map is not the territory.
confidence.note: Missing data reduces confidence. It never becomes zero silently, and it never gets invented.

build_gap.note: Positive: developers building faster than utility arrives. Promising or concerning depending on trajectory and Prove-It Age.

hype_gap.note: Attention scoring is Phase 2 (no reliable source in v0.1).

promise_gap.note: How much of the theoretical promise remains unrealized. One of the site's most important numbers.

potential_outlook.note: Forward-looking, but NOT a probability and NOT a price prediction — uncalibrated until historical backtesting exists (same rule as Execution Evidence). Reads as: of the promise not yet realized, how much does current execution support capturing? Floored at 0: a negative promise gap means the thesis is already exceeded, leaving no unrealized promise to capture.

gates.rationale: A protocol with ~zero demonstrated willingness-to-pay cannot sit in the top Reality tiers no matter how loud the narrative.
If the protocol works essentially unchanged without its token, the token's utility score cannot be high.
Low-confidence numbers must be labeled, not hidden.
gates.then: all score statuses for the project become 'provisional'

gates.rationale: Configured for Phase 2 when subsidy data exists. If >80% of activity disappears after incentives end, adoption components get capped.
gates.then: cap economic_throughput and thesis_milestones contributions at 50%

attention.description: Mindshare: mentions, search, social. Phase 2 — no reliable source in v0.1.
attention.name: Attention
attention.unavailable_reason: No reliable attention data source in v0.1 (X/Reddit/Trends adapters are Phase 2). Marked unavailable; reduces confidence.

development.description: Core-protocol development pace. Single-component in v0.1; expands with the GitHub adapter in Phase 2.
development.name: Development
development.note: GitHub stars have low weight by design; commits alone never dominate (both are gameable).

evidence_confidence.description: How much the numbers can be trusted, given data completeness and source quality.
evidence_confidence.name: Evidence Confidence

execution_evidence.description: Is the project measurably moving toward its potential? An evidence score — NOT a probability. No calibrated probabilities until historical backtesting exists (Phase 2).
execution_evidence.name: Execution Evidence

prove_it_age_years.description: Years since network launch. Not a countdown — there is no deadline. The question is: after X years, how much closer is the thesis to fulfilled?
prove_it_age_years.name: Prove-It Age

reality.components_note: Weights are per thesis category (see 'categories'). Weights of unavailable components are redistributed proportionally; confidence records the gap.
reality.description: Genuine utility demonstrated today: willingness to pay, capital committed, thesis milestones actually achieved. Market cap is NEVER an input — price is not evidence of utility.
reality.name: Reality

reflexivity_risk.description: How dependent the current value/ecosystem is on continued speculation, incentives, issuance, or belief. High score = high dependence. Characteristics are measured; projects are never labeled.
reflexivity_risk.name: Reflexivity / Failure Risk

subsidy_dependence.description: What happens to activity when incentives end (30/90/180-day post-incentive retention). No reliable source in v0.1.
subsidy_dependence.name: Subsidy Dependence
subsidy_dependence.unavailable_reason: Post-incentive retention data has no reliable source in v0.1. Marked unavailable; reduces confidence.

token_necessity.description: If the token disappeared, could essentially the same protocol continue functioning? Analyst-assessed, versioned, rationale published.
token_necessity.name: Token Necessity

token_value_capture.description: As usage grows, does the token capture economic value? Assessed against the mechanism checklist (fees, burns, staking, collateral, settlement demand). Successful protocol != valuable token until demonstrated.
token_value_capture.name: Token Value Capture

world_impact_potential.description: If the thesis succeeds, how consequential? Potential, not prediction. Analyst-assessed per thesis category, rationale published.
world_impact_potential.name: World Impact Potential

observer_effect.statement: Publishing scores can move markets. The Clock measures reflexivity risk in others; it must not become a source of it. Influence is a liability to be managed, not a goal.
observer_effect.goodharts_law: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. If projects ever optimize for Clock scores instead of real utility, the methodology must change — publicly, as a new version.

safeguards.text: Score history is append-only. New methodology versions add new snapshots; past snapshots are never rewritten.
Every scoring change ships as a new versioned methodology file. Diffs are public; silent rewrites are a defect, not a feature.
The publisher discloses positions in and promotional interest around scored tokens (see data/disclosures.json). Undisclosed holdings would make this a marketing operation, not a measurement one.
Algorithms calculate; nothing is tuned per-project. Every number comes from (methodology config + observations + versioned analyst seeds).
Paid placement and sponsorship never affect rankings.
